column2: Marianna Dwight to Anna Parsons on the end of Brook Farm (epigraph quoted by Duberman)
The salary committee writes to Holt: the financial strain comes from expansion spending; protest against the burden placed on the faculty
Report of the second committee (curriculum; Rice a member), which deepens Holt's anger
The AAUP investigating committee (Arthur O. Lovejoy, Austin S. Edwards) arrives at Rollins; Holt has gathered sworn statements from 22 students and 37 faculty members, employees and residents
Ten days of AAUP hearings at Rollins
AAUP hearing in the vestry of the Rollins chapel: Holt reads the statements, Rice replies (jockstrap, chisel, Plato…); Rice is accompanied by Lounsbury and Georgia
Preliminary report by Lovejoy and Edwards; the same day, Holt's “confidential memo” to the trustees accuses the investigators
End of Holt's purge: eight faculty members dismissed, asked to resign, or resigning, among them Georgia and Lounsbury (“ringleaders”)
Certificate of incorporation: the faculty is the sole member of the corporation; a Board of Fellows of six members elected for three years
Signing of the lease with the Blue Ridge Assembly for the rental of its buildings
First meeting of the incorporators; first Board of Fellows: Georgia, Lounsbury, Rice, Theodore Dreier, John Dreier, J. E. Spurr (terms drawn by lot: 1, 2, 3 years)
Theodore Dreier to Edward Corsi (Commissioner of Immigration) about the Alberses' visas
Edward Corsi to Theodore Dreier (the Alberses' visas)
Rice to Lovejoy: “the trouble really started” with the curriculum committee
First meeting of the Board of Fellows (half an hour, four present): Ted Dreier treasurer; Georgia, Lounsbury, Rice professors, Dreier associate professor
Joe Martin arrives at the Black Mountain station (met by Rice, then Bill Hinckley; Meg Hinckley takes him into town to buy butter)
Arrival of the faculty and the 22 students (14 from Rollins; Gary McGraw the only student from the area, a day student); they settle into Lee Hall, families in the cottages
First faculty meeting (the four resident members of the Board): five hours on the draft bylaws, adjourned to October 28
Special meeting of the Board of Fellows on the office of rector: Frederick Georgia chosen (Rice set aside until the AAUP report is published)
Memorial service for Ralph Lounsbury at Black Mountain College; statement by Georgia (“the integrity of the teaching profession was being assailed”)
Adjourned faculty meeting (Rice, Dreier, Georgia): adoption of the “Bylaws of Black Mountain College” (six pages); Board of Fellows, Advisory Council, secretary, rector elected for one year
Rice to Wunsch (invitation)

Special meeting of the Board (Rice, Dreier, Georgia): formal election to the faculty of Evarts, Martin, Hinckley, Helen Boyden, Hilda “Peggy” Loram, Emmy Zastrow, John Keith; room and board, no salary
Faculty meeting: on Rice's motion, a committee to study admission requirements
Ted Dreier's speech to the Black Mountain Women’s Club (“we would not make any important decision affecting the students without consulting them”)
Board meeting: tuition set at $340, plus $340 for board

Josef and Anni Albers arrive at Black Mountain a few days before Thanksgiving (Nov. 30, 1933); Rice meets them at the station; reception at Lee Hall (students prepared by Emmy Zastrow's “German table”); Albers: “I want to open eyes”
Josef Albers begins teaching (drawing, Werklehre); Anni Albers has neither looms nor students (Georgia builds her floor looms)
Robert Wunsch visits Black Mountain for Thanksgiving and finds there the hatred of Rollins
Ted Dreier to the members of the Board: the unpaid fees will probably not all be recovered
The faculty unanimously adopts the admission requirements (interview, special examination, certificate); samples of work encouraged; “special students” on Peggy Loram's motion
Board meeting: Dreier's projected budget (rent $4,500, heating $4,200, food $7,000, scholarships $3,800, salaries $1,875 not counting Albers's $1,000; total about $32,000); $1,000 voted to Albers
Rice to Janet Seasongood: stop hesitating between Smith and Black Mountain
Lecture by Thornton Wilder, “Relations of Literature and Life,” before the whole college and 250 outside guests
Rice to Elmer Davis on the Lincoln School
Amendments to the bylaws: access to all records, a student constitution, student officers present at meetings, the Student Moderator a member of the Board of Fellows
Rice to Wunsch
Adjourned Board meeting: revised budget (+$2,000, mostly for scholarships)
Rice to Aydelotte (on Georgia and the rectorship)
Editorial by Walter Locke on BMC, Dayton (Ohio) Daily News
Wunsch visits again for Thanksgiving: “the college on its own feet”; he is enthusiastic
Meeting on the role of the students
Student meeting: $816 already collected for Wunsch's salary
Adjourned Board meeting: fees raised ($1,200 all inclusive by the third year)
Goldenson to “Charles” on the college's visitors
Special meeting of the Board: salaries for the year voted ($7,250 for 17 people; Rice $1,600, Albers and Wunsch $1,000, seven members including Martin and Mangold $100)
Mangold to Rice (death of a conference-goer)
Mangold to Rice (“nine hundred vegetarian nincompoops”)
Dreier to Mangold on the fall reopening (clearing out the conference-goers, unpacking the equipment stored in the attic)
Mangold to Dreier (reopening)
Mangold to David Bailey (castration of the pig)
Letter from Mexico signed “L” offering the college a third of $285,000 if it gets him out of prison
Adamic to Rice
Rice to Adamic (then February 10)
Evarts's diary on the New York Herald Tribune article (an interview with Rice, in a “How-much-better-we-are” tone)
Gaynor Maddox to Rice (a favorable column read by two million people)

The Mondrian prank: Evarts and Allan Sly replace the Mondrian lent to Mort Steinau (Katherine Dreier collection) with a board covered in oilcloth; Albers furious, a student meeting, the painting found within a few hours
Diary of “John Doe” on physical attraction and self-control
Evening discussion in a student's room: Rice tells of meeting Edgar Lee Masters at the Deweys'; “turning out a Black Mountain type”

General meeting: Adamic reads his article on BMC; debate late into the night: Martin, Evarts, George Hendrickson, George Barber (“too damn many sheep”), Nat French, Wunsch, Robert Goldenson (“we need a little Jesus”); Rice: “The worst sin in the world is impatience… make yourselves into little anti-Rices”
Mangold to “John and Dasa” on the Adamic meeting
Adamic to Rice: DeVoto's article is “a scream”
Rice to Gaynor Maddox
Board meeting: salaries (followed by the meetings of Oct. 23, Nov. 30, Dec. 18, 1936)
DeVoto to Lewis Gannett (a furious reply; Gannett had defended BMC in the Herald-Tribune)
Mangold to Louis Adamic (where the students come from)
Board of Fellows meeting: Rice, Albers, Dreier, Mangold and Mary Beaman (Student Moderator) vote a pessimistic warning to Knickerbocker and Goldenson; Georgia and Martin against
Letter from the Board (signed by Georgia, secretary) to Knickerbocker: “quite pessimistic” about his ability to become a permanent faculty member
A student approaches Rice as he is digging potatoes: “You just fired Knickerbocker”; uproar in the college
Rice to Louis Adamic on the Bennington visit
Rice to Adamic: he “had not foreseen” the Board's decision
Mangold to Adamic (the Knickerbocker affair)
Rice to Henry Allen Moe
Lewis Gannett to Adamic: BMC is “a means,” not a community that is an end in itself
Mangold to “Augusto”
General meeting: 14 of the 15 faculty members and 42 of the 49 students speak
Student meeting on the “agreements” (Harrington, French, Stella, Seasongood); “Why isn’t a bedroom an infirmary?”
One-page photo story in the “Fotogravure” section of the Sunday New York Times (“Horrid, misleading as hell”); 50 to 55 letters in the first week
Neal Van Middlesworth to Mangold on the letters prompted by the Times (“Dear Rollins Rebels”)
Mangold to Adamic
Mangold to Joseph Martin on the “Peter Sweeney” case
Four-page letter from Tasker Howard to the admissions committee on the “Peter Sweeney” case (released from a psychiatric hospital)
Martin to Mangold on Noguchi
Faculty meeting planned on teaching, postponed in Albers's absence
Faculty meeting on “what teaching is” (Rice, Albers, Martin, Portell, Zeuch, Dreier): instruction versus education, personality, disciples
Faculty meeting (the Knickerbocker-Goldenson affair)
Faculty meeting: Albers wants discussions of teaching without the student officers; Tasker Howard and John Harrington speak, then the student officers leave; James Gore King on bad teachers
Faculty meeting: “imperialism” in teaching (Albers, Rice, Zeuch, Schawinsky, Mangold)
Board meeting (salaries)
Faculty meeting: the limits of personality in education, “dangerous” personalities (Rice, Albers, Zeuch, Mangold, King, Martin, Schawinsky)
Board of Fellows meeting
Mangold to Adams (on Schawinsky)

Special faculty meeting demanded by Zeuch, with the student representatives, while Rice and Albers are away traveling: why is Knickerbocker being dismissed? Wunsch speaks of “two colleges”; the session runs late into the night
Zeuch's petition to the Board to reconsider the decision on Knickerbocker and Goldenson (rejected)

General meeting on governance: the dissident students (“organic democracy”: Harrington, George Alsberg…) against Rice (“a college” and not a community; “some people who are incompetent to have opinions”)
Rice to George Leighton on Hutchins and Mortimer Adler
Rice to Dean F. F. Bradshaw on social justice
The Board of Fellows receives the four students of the Florida trip (“Little came out of the meeting”)
The governing bodies place the four students in the care of Fred Mangold and Anna Moellenhoff
Student meeting: a provisional agreement, “mixed parties do not take vacations together”; no penalty
